title: Water Purification
summary: How to make raw water safe to drink using filtration, heat, chemicals, or sunlight.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Pre-Filter the Water
sections.body: Filter out large suspended particles like dirt, leaves, and debris. Pour the water through a clean cloth, coffee filter, or a layered sand-and-gravel survival filter. This improves the effectiveness of subsequent purification steps.
sections.warning: Pre-filtration only removes sediment. It does not remove microscopic pathogens.

sections.heading: Step 2 — Boil to Disinfect
sections.body: Bringing water to a rolling boil is the most effective method for killing disease-causing pathogens, including viruses, bacteria, and parasites. Keep water boiling for at least 1 full minute (or 3 minutes at altitudes above 2,000 meters / 6,500 feet). Let it cool naturally.
sections.warning: Boiling does not remove heavy metals or chemical toxins; it only kills biological pathogens.
sections.image_description: Water boiling in a pot over campfire

sections.heading: Step 3 — Chemical Treatment (Bleach or Iodine)
sections.body: If boiling is not possible, use unscented household chlorine bleach (5% to 9% sodium hypochlorite). Add 8 drops (approx. 0.5 mL) per gallon / 3.8 liters of clear water. Double the dose if the water is cloudy. Stir and let sit for 30 minutes before drinking. Alternatively, use commercial iodine or chlorine dioxide tablets.
sections.warning: Never use scented, color-safe, or splashless bleaches, as they contain toxic chemicals.
sections.image_description: Dropping bleach into a container of water

sections.heading: Step 4 — Solar Disinfection (SODIS)
sections.body: In sunny conditions, fill clean, transparent plastic bottles (PET bottles, under 2 liters) with pre-filtered water. Shake to oxygenate. Lay the bottles flat on a dark surface (such as metal sheeting) in direct sunlight for at least 6 hours (or 2 days if cloudy). The UV rays and heat will pasteurize the water.
sections.warning: Do not use glass or scratched plastic bottles, as they block UV light.
sections.image_description: Plastic bottles lying on a roof in the sun

when_to_use: When you must consume water from untreated natural sources like rivers, lakes, rainwater, or questionable wells.
do_not: Drink saltwater or brackish water (requires distillation)
Rely on filtration alone to kill viruses
Use toxic chemical products for disinfection
Drink untreated water even if it looks crystal clear
sources: World Health Organization Safe Water Guidelines
